# t17.1 — RED-first Layer/Port Architecture Rules

## Summary

Added two zero-exemption bytecode rules to `LayerDependencyRulesTest`:

- **Rule 3a:** production classes in `domain`, `application`,
  `infrastructure`, `presentation`, and `shared` cannot reference a type in
  the root package `dev.logicojp.reviewer`.
- **Rule 4a:** production types under `application.port` cannot reference
  application implementation types outside `application.port`.

The published rule identities remain stable. The new checks are 3a and 4a;
existing Rules 3, 4, and 4b were not renumbered.

## Deliverables

- [`batch-report.yaml`](./batch-report.yaml) — structured implementation and
  verification result.
- [`checkpoints/tasks-to-impl.yaml`](./checkpoints/tasks-to-impl.yaml) —
  current-batch requirement-to-implementation checkpoint.

## Scope and Boundaries

- Matched implementation-plan task: `T012` (dependency-direction enforcement).
- Production responsibilities and runtime behavior were not changed.
- The H1/H2 `ReviewApp` and `ApplicationPortFactory` responsibility split
  remains explicitly assigned to t17.2.
- No API endpoint contract applies; this repository builds a CLI application.

## Implementation

### Rule 3a — Named layers cannot depend on layer zero

- Analyzes all 339 compiled production classes in the five named layers.
- Independently enumerates 185 primary source types and proves each one is in
  the analyzed bytecode subject set.
- Rejects every dependency whose package is exactly
  `dev.logicojp.reviewer`; there is no allowlist.
- Uses a retained test-tree fixture with the exact H3 edge shape,
  `application.probe.T17RootReferenceViolation -> ReviewPortFactory`, to prove
  the detector remains live.

### Rule 4a — Ports cannot depend on application implementations

- Analyzes all 30 compiled production classes under `application.port`.
- Independently enumerates 26 primary port source types and proves each one is
  in the analyzed bytecode subject set.
- Allows dependencies within `application.port` but rejects every dependency
  to another `application.*` package; there is no allowlist.
- Uses a retained test-tree fixture with the exact H4 edge shape,
  `application.port.inbound.T17PortImplementationViolation ->
  application.policy.T17ApplicationPolicy`, to prove the detector remains
  live.

The permanent controls compile only into `target/test-classes`. Production
analysis remains rooted at `target/classes`, so the controls cannot pollute
the graph they validate.

## RED/GREEN Evidence

Both t17 mutant shapes were inserted separately into an isolated temporary
repository copy under `src/main/java` and exercised with Java 28.

| Mutation | Expected RED result | Restored result |
|---|---:|---:|
| Named layer → `ReviewPortFactory` | 19 run, exactly 1 Rule 3a failure | 19/19 pass |
| `application.port` → `application.policy` | 19 run, exactly 1 Rule 4a failure | 19/19 pass |

Each failure named both the violating owner and its target. After removing the
mutants, `src/main/java` in the temporary copy matched the real workspace
byte-for-byte. The temporary copy was then removed.
